title: Why a Mute Swan Sits on a Nest Beside Water

narration_timeline.text: Why is this mute swan sitting on a mound of sticks instead of swimming?
narration_timeline.scene: Close mute swan settled on a stick nest in Prague, visually reviewed.

narration_timeline.text: That raised spot is a nest, built close enough to water for the adults to reach.
narration_timeline.scene: Real mute swans and their eggs at a waterside nest.

narration_timeline.text: Away from the nest, mute swans travel along canals with other family members nearby.
narration_timeline.scene: Mute swan family including young swimming along a Wiltshire canal.

narration_timeline.text: The water lets them move and feed, while the bank offers a place to rest.
narration_timeline.scene: Mute swan in a Slovenian park near water; feeding not claimed visible.

narration_timeline.text: Back near shore, a swan may settle into its nest while another moves across the pond.
narration_timeline.scene: Two swans walking on foggy bank and a separate Drage pond scene.

narration_timeline.text: From nesting to resting on shore, swans also fly over the water that connects their daily routines.
narration_timeline.scene: Actual mute swans resting on grass, followed by a distinct real flock flying over water. No invented takeoff or nest scene in these shots.
